validity.recommendation: No existence, duplicate, or classification concern. TransColorado Gas Transmission Company LLC is a real, currently-operating FERC-jurisdictional interstate pipeline running from the Piceance/San Juan supply basins in northwest Colorado (Rio Blanco County) south to the San Juan Basin in northwest New Mexico (San Juan County), where it interconnects with El Paso Natural Gas and other systems. Confirmed independently via: (1) Kinder Morgan's own current (2026) corporate website listing it as an active wholly-owned natural gas pipeline asset; (2) two 1996/1998 Federal Register notices (FERC dockets CP95-79 and related) describing the same 22/24-inch, ~311-mile pipeline between the same two counties; (3) Kinder Morgan Inc.'s FY2012 SEC Form 10-K, which lists TransColorado among its wholly-owned gas pipeline assets with a 1.0 Bcf/d capacity figure; (4) El Paso Natural Gas Company's own 1996 SEC Form 10-Q, filed when El Paso still held a one-third ownership interest, independently corroborating the ~311-mile length and construction timeline; (5) offshore-technology.com/GlobalData profile; (6) Wikipedia. It is correctly classified as a distinct pipeline, NOT a duplicate of the two other 'Kinder Morgan Rockies trio' FERC systems flagged in the batch brief -- Colorado Interstate Gas (P0168) and Wyoming Interstate Company (P0282) are separate FERC-regulated entities/pipelines with their own certificated routes; none of the sources found for P0270 mention CIG or WIC facilities, and vice versa in cross-checks. CAVEAT (not escalated to a concern): offshore-technology.com's auto-generated 'location' schema snippet erroneously labels BOTH termini as 'Colorado' -- this is judged to be a GlobalData template/boilerplate artifact, contradicted by the weight of more precise, independent evidence (Kinder Morgan's own site, the 1996/1998 Federal Register notices, and Wikipedia) that consistently places the southern/eastern terminus in San Juan County, New Mexico. Ownership has consolidated over time from an original 1994-1995 three-way partnership (KN Energy Inc., Questar Pipeline Co., and El Paso Natural Gas Co., after El Paso bought Public Service Company of Colorado's original one-third stake in 1995) into a wholly-owned Kinder Morgan asset (KN Energy became Kinder Morgan Inc. via merger) -- this ownership evolution is historical background, not a current attribution error; GEM's Owner1='Kinder Morgan' 100% is CURRENT and correct.
